name: DNSCrypt Proxy
description: Smart DNS filtering with DNSCrypt. Local resolver on 127.0.0.1:5354 with per-profile blocklists (HaGeZi Light/Normal/PRO/PRO++/Ultimate), wildcard-aware Custom Rules (Allowlist + Denylist), WebUI (English default + Arabic toggle), separate monitoring Dashboard with JSON metrics, SSE live updates, and offline-capable PWA. Zero telemetry. v1.1.0 added dynamic per-profile memory limits (light=80MB to ultimate=220MB), extended shellQuote charset, and the MONITORING_UI_PORT constant. v1.2.0 adds comprehensive user-data preservation: multi-source smart detection (7 candidate locations — 9 on APatch, which adds two modules_update paths), persistent backup in /sdcard/dnscrypt-webui-backup, SHA256 integrity verification, transactional atomic upgrades with auto-rollback, recovery mode via trigger file, root-solution compatibility (Magisk/KernelSU/APatch), SELinux context preservation, periodic and pre-critical auto-backup, backup rotation (max 21 copies), upgrade history log, and a CLI diagnose tool.
author: gasciljh

shortcuts.name: Control Panel
shortcuts.description: Open the WebUI landing page (same origin as the manifest)

shortcuts.name: Monitoring Dashboard
shortcuts.description: Open the Dashboard landing page (same origin as the manifest)

x-note-shortcuts: Per the PWA spec, shortcut URLs MUST be same-origin with the manifest's start_url. Because the WebUI (default port 9090) and Dashboard (default port 9091) are DIFFERENT origins, a single manifest CANNOT provide cross-origin shortcuts. Both shortcuts therefore use RELATIVE URLs (/?source=shortcut_webui and /?source=shortcut_dashboard) that resolve to the manifest's CURRENT origin. Consequence: when the PWA is installed from port 9090, both shortcuts open the WebUI; when installed from port 9091, both shortcuts open the Dashboard. The shortcut LABEL may therefore not match the page that opens. For reliable cross-origin navigation, the WebUI provides a dynamic Dashboard link built from /api?action=runtime_info (fields webui_port, dashboard_port) — see the v1.0.0 PORT-2 fix in index.html and dashboard.html. Users who want a Dashboard-specific PWA shortcut should install the PWA from port 9091 separately, which gives the Dashboard its own app icon and shortcuts. Prior versions used absolute URLs (http://127.0.0.1:9090 and :9091) which are cross-origin and are silently rejected by browsers that enforce the PWA spec. Full rationale: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6.6.
x-note-port-limitation: For dynamic port handling, the WebUI/Dashboard HTML/JS read the actual ports from /api?action=runtime_info (fields: webui_port, dashboard_port) and construct URLs dynamically. However, PWA shortcuts (this section) are evaluated by the browser BEFORE any JS runs, so they cannot benefit from runtime_info. See v1.0.0 PORT-2 fix in index.html and dashboard.html for the dynamic link implementation.
x-note-ports: Default ports: WebUI=9090, Dashboard=9091. Monitoring UI (internal): 8080. DNS Engine: 5354. All ports are configurable in webui.conf except 8080 (reserved for dnscrypt-proxy's monitoring_ui).
x-note-screenshots: The 'screenshots' array was intentionally removed in v1.0.0. Per PWA spec, screenshots should be actual app screenshots (not icons). Add real screenshots in a future release to enable Chrome's richer install UI.
x-note-maskable: The 'maskable' purpose currently reuses /icon-512.png. The maskable safe zone is a circle of radius 40% of the canvas (approximately 205 px in a 512 canvas). The shield extends from y=52 to y=448 — right at the top boundary (51.2). Horizontal extent (x=96 to x=416) is safely inside. Result: renders fine on most Android launchers, but may be clipped on devices with aggressive circular masks (45%+). A future release (v1.3.0) will ship a purpose-built maskable SVG/PNG with a wider safe-zone margin. See web/icon-512.svg header for the full analysis and docs/ROADMAP.md §5.1 for tracking. M-1 note (v1.2.0): the duplicate /icon-512.png entry above (one 'any', one 'maskable') is intentional and spec-compliant; it will be replaced by a dedicated /icon-maskable.png when v1.3.0 lands.
x-note-version: The 'version' field is not standard in the PWA manifest spec but is used here for documentation/troubleshooting. It mirrors the VERSION file for consistency. As of v1.3.0 it is '1.3.0' (no 'v' prefix, per PWA convention). This value is checked by .github/workflows/ci.yml → 'Verify version consistency' step.
x-note-runtime-info: The /api?action=runtime_info endpoint returns the following schema. Build info (since v1.0.0): 'version', 'commit', 'build_time', 'build_time_human', 'project_url'. Runtime paths (v1.0.0): 'run_dir', 'status_file', 'pid_file', 'progress_file', 'log_file'. Network (v1.0.0): 'bind_addr'. Dynamic ports (v1.0.0, PORT-2): 'webui_port', 'dashboard_port'. Memory profile (v1.1.0, MEM-1): 'profile_key' (light/normal/pro/proplus/ultimate), 'memory_limit_mb' (Go runtime soft memory limit for that profile). Backups (v1.2.0, BAK-1): a nested 'backups' object with SEVEN fields — see x-note-backup-schema below for the exact schema.
x-note-backup-schema: The 'backups' object returned by /api?action=runtime_info contains SEVEN fields (v1.2.0, BAK-1). This aligns main.go's schema with the one already produced by status.sh --json, so both endpoints can be consumed by clients using the same field names: (1) 'available' — int, number of snapshots excluding current/, txn-*, and orphan-txn-*; (2) 'in_flight_txn' — int, number of txn-* directories (install in progress or interrupted); (3) 'orphan_txn' — int, number of orphan-txn-* directories (preserved interrupted installs, user-managed); (4) 'last_backup' — string|null, timestamp of the newest snapshot in 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' format; (5) 'last_backup_name' — string|null, directory name of the newest snapshot (e.g. '20260926-150000-manual-12345-a1b2'); (6) 'last_stable' — string|null, content of the .last_stable pointer file; (7) 'path' — string, absolute path of the persistent backup directory ('/sdcard/dnscrypt-webui-backup'). Note: status.sh --json additionally exposes two diagnostic-only fields ('status' and 'last_backup_age_seconds') that are NOT part of the API surface. The WebUI and Dashboard System Info panels display six of the seven fields (all except 'last_backup', the raw timestamp).
x-note-memory: As of v1.1.0, main.go sets the Go runtime soft memory limit dynamically based on the active blocklist profile: light=80MB, normal=100MB, pro=120MB, proplus=160MB, ultimate=220MB. debug.SetMemoryLimit is a SOFT limit: the runtime prefers running GC more aggressively over OOMing. The manifest itself is unaffected by this behavior.
x-note-backup: As of v1.2.0, the installer (customize.sh) and runtime (service.sh, main.go) preserve the 5 user config files (webui.conf, dnscrypt-proxy.toml, selected_profile.txt, allowlist.txt, denylist.txt) across upgrades, renames, reinstalls, and uninstalls. Backups are stored at /sdcard/dnscrypt-webui-backup/ and survive module removal. The manifest does not need to know about this — it is a runtime concern on the device. See docs/BACKUP.md and docs/EMERGENCY.md for the full model.
x-note-backup-paths: Persistent backup directory: /sdcard/dnscrypt-webui-backup/. Subdirectories (all include a PID suffix added in v1.2.0 to prevent second-level timestamp collisions): 'current/' (live snapshot, always up to date), '<timestamp>-<version>-<pid>/' (historical snapshots written by customize.sh during install — BUG-CS-C fix), '<timestamp>-manual-<pid>/' (pre-critical snapshots written by functions.sh:backup_user_files — FSH-10 fix), '<timestamp>-manual-<pid>-<rand4>/' (pre-critical snapshots written by main.go:createAutoBackup with an additional random suffix — BUG-E fix), '<timestamp>-auto-<pid>/' (periodic snapshots written by service.sh via functions.sh:auto_backup_if_needed — FSH-10 fix), 'txn-<timestamp>-<pid>/' (in-flight transactions, cleaned up automatically), 'orphan-txn-<timestamp>-<pid>/' (preserved interrupted installs, user-managed). Metadata files: '.last_stable' (pointer to the last known good snapshot), '.upgrade_history.json' (full upgrade log, written when jq is available), '.upgrade_history.txt' (fallback log when jq is unavailable), '.last_auto_backup' (mtime marker for the periodic 24-hour auto-backup), '.pending_notification' (transient message written by customize.sh after a restore, read and deleted by main.go at startup), 'README.md' (user guide). Rotation caps at 21 snapshots by directory name.
x-note-recovery: As of v1.2.0, a recovery mode can be triggered by creating a file at /data/adb/modules/dnscrypt-proxy-webui/recovery (or /data/adb/dnscrypt-recovery) and rebooting. The installer will restore the last known good configuration from the persistent backup. The recovery priority is: (1) .last_stable pointer, (2) current/ live snapshot, (3) in-place data. The in-module trigger (recovery) is deleted by customize.sh after a successful recovery; the external trigger (/data/adb/dnscrypt-recovery) is also removed by uninstall.sh (UNI-1 fix). See docs/EMERGENCY.md for step-by-step instructions.
x-note-icon-source: Icon generation pipeline (verified against scripts/generate-icons.sh): icon-192.svg produces icon-192.png (192x192); icon-512.svg produces icon-512.png (512x512), apple-touch-icon.png (180x180), favicon-32x32.png (32x32), and favicon-16x16.png (16x16); favicon-16x16.png + favicon-32x32.png produce favicon.ico (multi-size). IMPORTANT: icon-192.png is generated from icon-192.svg, NOT from icon-512.svg. Prior documentation incorrectly claimed icon-512.svg was the source for all PNGs — corrected in v1.1.0 in both icon-512.svg header and this note. HARD-MF-02 note (v1.2.0): the full filenames favicon-16x16.png and favicon-32x32.png are used here (parity with scripts/generate-icons.sh, HARD-GIC-02).
x-note-language: The WebUI ships with English as the DEFAULT language and an in-page toggle (langToggle) that switches to Arabic. This is the 'global edition' policy: a single canonical default (English) plus first-class access for Arabic-speaking users without requiring a fork. The 'lang' field of this manifest defaults to 'en' and 'dir' to 'ltr'; the in-page toggle switches them to 'ar'/'rtl' at runtime. The user's preference is stored client-side in localStorage['dnscrypt-lang'] and is NEVER transmitted to the server. Documentation remains English-only by project convention; community translations are welcome as separate files (docs/*.<lang>.md). Additional WebUI languages (FR, DE, ES, RU, ZH, ...) are deferred to v1.4.0 — see docs/ROADMAP.md §6.

x-note-pre-release-audit-v120: A pre-release audit of the manifest identified the following issues, all addressed in-place without a version bump. (1) MAN-1: x-note-backup-paths was missing '.pending_notification' from its list of metadata files. That file is written by customize.sh after a successful restore during an upgrade and read/deleted by main.go at boot; it is part of the documented backup-directory structure in customize.sh §22, functions.sh, and ARCHITECTURE.md §8.1. The field now lists it. (2) MAN-2 + MAN-3: both PWA shortcuts (Control Panel, Monitoring Dashboard) used ABSOLUTE URLs pointing to http://127.0.0.1:9090 and http://127.0.0.1:9091 respectively. Per the PWA spec, shortcut URLs MUST be same-origin with the manifest's start_url. Because WebUI (9090) and Dashboard (9091) are different origins, the Dashboard shortcut was cross-origin and would be silently rejected by browsers that enforce the spec. Even on browsers that tolerate it, the shortcut would open a hardcoded 127.0.0.1 address that fails when the user accesses the WebUI via a LAN IP (e.g. 192.168.1.5:9090). Both shortcuts have been changed to RELATIVE URLs (/?source=shortcut_webui and /?source=shortcut_dashboard) which resolve to the manifest's current origin. The known consequence — both shortcuts open the current origin's landing page, which may not match the label when installed from port 9091 — is now documented explicitly in x-note-shortcuts. For reliable cross-origin navigation between WebUI and Dashboard, the WebUI's dashboardLink already reads /api?action=runtime_info and builds the correct URL dynamically (v1.0.0 PORT-2 fix). (3) x-note-shortcuts was rewritten to describe the same-origin requirement, the new relative URLs, the label/page-may-mismatch caveat, the LAN-IP scenario, and the recommended workaround (install a second PWA from port 9091 for a Dashboard-specific shortcut).
x-note-global-edition-v120: Global Edition additions to the manifest (same release, no version bump). (1) HARD-MF-01: x-note-backup-paths now explicitly lists the PID suffix on every snapshot directory name, matching the actual on-device naming produced by customize.sh (BUG-CS-C), main.go (BUG-E), functions.sh (FSH-10), and action.sh (ACT-5). (2) HARD-MF-02: x-note-icon-source now uses the full filenames favicon-16x16.png and favicon-32x32.png instead of the abbreviated favicon-16.png / favicon-32.png (parity with the same correction in scripts/generate-icons.sh, HARD-GIC-02). (3) HARD-MF-03: the description field now states '9 on APatch' in addition to '7 candidate locations', matching the actual candidate list in customize.sh [8] (parity with README.md). (4) L-1 (cleanup): 'browser' was removed from display_override — including it would have overridden 'standalone' as the effective fallback, defeating the purpose of the field. (5) L-3 (cleanup): 'productivity' was removed from categories — a DNS proxy is a network utility / security tool, not a productivity app. (6) L-5 (cleanup): this section and x-note-pre-release-audit-v120 were split into two separate x-note fields to end the previous numbering confusion (MAN-3 appeared twice under a single list).
